findings: The draw's control is only faintly seen: with food, a crowd drawing prey by members alone differed from the exact runner on one reading of 34 (Holm p 0.017, distance 0.029); with water, on none of 44 (smallest Holm p 0.11). The certified comparison includes the draw, and the crowd matches it, but its readings say little about how prey are chosen at this domain's predation.

Prey running out part way through a site's hunters is the one place the core's identity order reaches a hunt's outcome. The crowd matches it only when those hunters share one state; in this domain they always did (a site's hunters are founded in one cohort), about once in 200 draws. Ruling 269's scramble, part of Part B, would remove the identity order.
The crowd saves fewer evaluations than at checkpoint 1 at every density, because both runners now skip what the scheduler's filing skips.
